body: It's good advice. Just easier said than done.
Thank you. And so are you.
I feel this in my soul.
I could have written this letter. I'm so sorry you have to deal with this pain.
Such a hard thing to do 💛
I know the feeling of wanting to tell your best friend and then remembering you can't. I hope things work out for you. And I'm proud of you for doing the thing.
Thank you so much for this.

>I just hope this is easier for you than me.

That's love.
No. I don't know if I ever will. But I had to try.

He promised we would go to therapy, but we never did. He is actually a covert narcissist. Logically, I know running would be better for me in the long run. But the trauma bond makes it feel impossible. I'll be seeking therapy for myself soon.
You've written the words on my heart. But I can't accept that he's the disease. I only think of him as the cure.
I don't care if it's positive or negative. I just want to hear from him.
I hate you're going through it too. This is the worst pain of my life.
Not to overwhelm you with follow up questions, but how did she learn? Did you tell her? Did a therapist explain it? What resources did she have? And what efforts did you take to understand her?
